chunks: Muhammad b. Ali (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi al-Qasim narrated to me. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas'ada b. Ziyad from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad from his father from his forefathers (peace be upon them). He said: Ali (peace be upon him) said:

Surely, a Muslim person has three friends: A friend that says to him: 'I am with you, alive and dead' — that is his deeds. A friend that says to him: 'I am with you until you die' — that is his wealth, for when he dies, it goes to the heirs. And a friend that says to him: 'I am with you until the gateway of your grave, then I will leave you' — that is his child.

key_terms.عَمَلُهُ: his deeds, referring to good and bad actions that follow a person to the afterlife
key_terms.وَرَثَة: heirs, those who inherit wealth after death

ai.seo_question: What are the three friends of every Muslim according to Imam Ali (as)?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (as) teaches that every Muslim has three companions in life: deeds, wealth, and children. Only deeds accompany a person both in life and in death, while wealth transfers to heirs upon death, and children only escort one to the grave. This teaching emphasizes the priority of righteous actions over material possessions and family ties.

en.bilal-muhammad: Muhammad b. `Ali (rh) narrated to us. He said: My uncle Muhammad b. Abi’l Qasim narrated to me. He said: Harun b. Muslim narrated to us from Mas`ada b. Ziyad from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad form his father from his forefathers (as). He said: `Ali (as) said:

Surely, a Muslim person has three friends: (1) A friend that says to him: “I am with you, alive and dead” – that is his deeds. (2) A friend that says to him: “I am with you until you die” – that is his wealth, for when he dies, it is given in inheritance. (3) A friend that says to him: “I am with you until the gateway of your grave, then I will leave you” – that is his child.
